title: Short signup profiling to test 'wrong-fit signups'
decision_task: What to ask at signup and how to route users to self-serve, automated help or a human.
applies_when: Self-serve signups with mixed intent (personal vs work, small vs larger companies)
Activation is the constraint and the competing explanation is wrong-fit signups
B2B products where some signups merit sales or onboarding help
exclusions: A question will not change any segment, message or route
Teams of two or fewer (skip the team-invite step)
required_inputs: Ability to add closed-answer questions to signup
Privacy notice covering what is collected
evidence_requirements: Whether any human help capacity exists
missing_data_behavior: No segment data: add 1-3 closed questions; the next diagnosis reads activation in the target segment.
alternatives_when_constrained: Missing data: start with one question (work vs personal)
Low traffic: owner reviews each signup's answers by hand
No integration: add a field to the existing signup form
Small budget: avoid paid enrichment; for small businesses and consumers she finds it mostly wrong

decision_branches.if: A question won't change a segment, message or route
Some signups merit a human and the owner has stated capacity

implementation_steps: Ask use (work or personal), role, and new vs migrating
Ask company size or industry only for work use and only if used
Offer a team invite for teams above two
Ask the job they came to do with closed options plus 'something else'
Segment activation and paid by answers
Route: migrations or high-value signups to a human; small gaps to in-app or email help; readers to docs
metrics: Profiling completion and drop-off vs prior baseline
Activation and paid rate by segment
guardrails: Collect only what is used and disclose it
Measure drop-off rather than assume her 10–15% figure
observation_window: Until each key segment has enough signups to compare activation; state the count before starting.
stop_conditions: Drop-off at profiling clearly above prior baseline and total activated users fall: shorten
No segment differs in activation: profiling adds no decision value, cut to one question
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: shared/agents/diagnosis.ts COMPETING.activation (wrong-fit signups); PB-activation-repair; Book 08 §5 segmentation.

interpretation: INTERPRETATION: diagnosis.ts already names wrong-fit signups as the competing explanation for weak activation but gives no way to test it. Profiling is that test.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: When the constraint is activation and no segment data exists, the plan's first step adds one to three closed profiling questions and the next diagnosis reads activation within the target segment. Routing to a human requires stated owner capacity.
disagreements: Common advice to minimize onboarding questions conflicts with her view that a short structured profile costs little. Treat her drop-off figures as untested hypotheses and measure.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
expected_behavior: Computes activation within the target segment (22%) vs overall (10%)
Concludes the low headline rate is mostly signup mix and moves effort toward targeting or positioning, while still checking work-user activation
Keeps the profiling short and closed-answer
hard_failure: Recommends rebuilding onboarding for all users without segmenting
Makes paid third-party enrichment the primary data source for small businesses

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
